sanskrit: lomaharṣaṇaputra ugraśravāḥ sūtaḥ paurāṇiko naimiṣāraṇye śaunakasya kulapater dvādaśavārṣike satre
english: Ugraśravā, the son of Lomaharṣaṇa, a sūta versed in the Purāṇas, came once to the twelve-year sacrificial session of Śaunaka, lord of the kula, in the Naimiṣa forest.

sanskrit: samāsīnān abhyagacchad brahmarṣīn saṃśitavratān vinayāvanato bhūtvā kadā cit sūtanandanaḥ
english: The son of the sūta approached the brahmarṣis who were seated there, those of sharpened vows, bowing humbly before them.

sanskrit: tam āśramam anuprāptaṃ naimiṣāraṇyavāsinaḥ citrāḥ śrotuṃ kathās tatra parivavrus tapasvinaḥ
english: When he arrived at that hermitage, the ascetics dwelling in the Naimiṣa forest gathered around him, eager to hear his wondrous tales.

sanskrit: abhivādya munīṃs tāṃs tu sarvān eva kṛtāñjaliḥ apṛcchat sa tapovṛddhiṃ sadbhiś caivābhinanditaḥ
english: Having saluted all those sages with palms joined, he enquired after the progress of their austerities, and was in turn warmly greeted by those good men.

sanskrit: atha teṣūpaviṣṭeṣu sarveṣv eva tapasviṣu nirdiṣṭam āsanaṃ bheje vinayāl lomaharṣaṇiḥ
english: When all the ascetics had taken their seats, Lomaharṣaṇi humbly took the seat that had been indicated for him.

sanskrit: sukhāsīnaṃ tatas taṃ tu viśrāntam upalakṣya ca athāpṛcchad ṛṣis tatra kaś cit prastāvayan kathāḥ
english: Seeing him comfortably seated and rested, a certain ṛṣi then asked him a question, setting the conversation in motion.

sanskrit: kuta āgamyate saute kva cāyaṃ vihṛtas tvayā kālaḥ kamalapatrākṣa śaṃsaitat pṛcchato mama
english: "From where have you come, O Sauta? And where has this time been spent by you? O lotus-eyed one, tell me this, for I am asking."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca janamejayasya rājarṣeḥ sarpasatre mahātmanaḥ samīpe pārthivendrasya samyak pārikṣitasya ca
english: The sūta said: "I was in the presence of the royal sage Janamejaya, son of Parīkṣit, that great-souled lord among the Pārthas, at his snake sacrifice."

sanskrit: kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaproktāḥ supuṇyāḥ vividhāḥ kathāḥ kathitāś cāpi vidhivad yā vaiśaṃpāyanena vai
english: "The highly meritorious and various tales spoken by Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana were duly recited there by Vaiśaṃpāyana as well."

sanskrit: śrutvāhaṃ tā vicitrārthā mahābhāratasaṃśritāḥ bahūni saṃparikramya tīrthāny āyatanāni ca
english: "Having heard those stories of varied meaning, rooted in the Mahābhārata, and having visited many tīrthas and sacred shrines in pilgrimage,"

sanskrit: samantapañcakaṃ nāma puṇyaṃ dvijaniṣevitam gatavān asmi taṃ deśaṃ yuddhaṃ yatrābhavat purā pāṇḍavānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ ca mahīkṣitām
english: "I went to that holy place frequented by the twice-born, named Samantapañcaka, where in former times the great battle of the Pāṇḍavas and the Kurus, and all the kings of the earth, took place."

sanskrit: didṛkṣur āgatas tasmāt samīpaṃ bhavatām iha āyuṣmantaḥ sarva eva brahmabhūtā hi me matāḥ
english: "Wishing to see you, I have come from there to your presence. O long-lived ones, you are all, in my view, become Brahman itself."

sanskrit: asmin yajñe mahābhāgāḥ sūryapāvakavarcasaḥ kṛtābhiṣekāḥ śucayaḥ kṛtajapyā hutāgnayaḥ bhavanta āsate svasthā bravīmi kim ahaṃ dvijāḥ
english: "O highly fortunate ones, blazing with the splendour of the sun and fire, purified by ritual baths, pure, having completed your mutterings and fed the fires — you sit here at ease. What shall I speak to you, O twice-born ones?"

sanskrit: purāṇasaṃśritāḥ puṇyāḥ kathā vā dharmasaṃśritāḥ itivṛttaṃ narendrāṇām ṛṣīṇāṃ ca mahātmanām
english: "Sacred tales rooted in the Purāṇas, or tales rooted in dharma, the histories of kings and of great-souled ṛṣis —"

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ dvaipāyanena yat proktaṃ purāṇaṃ paramarṣiṇā surair brahmarṣibhiś caiva śrutvā yad abhipūjitam
english: The ṛṣis said: "That Purāṇa proclaimed by Dvaipāyana, the supreme ṛṣi, which the gods and the brahmarṣis heard and honoured —"

sanskrit: tasyākhyānavariṣṭhasya vicitrapadaparvaṇaḥ sūkṣmārthanyāyayuktasya vedārthair bhūṣitasya ca
english: "— that which is foremost among narratives, with its varied words and cantos, endowed with subtle meanings and reasoning, adorned with the purport of the Vedas —"

sanskrit: bhāratasyetihāsasya puṇyāṃ granthārthasaṃyutām saṃskāropagatāṃ brāhmīṃ nānāśāstropabṛṃhitām
english: "— the holy Bhārata itihāsa, united with the meaning of its text, elevated by refinement, spoken in the language of Brahmā, enriched by various śāstras —"

sanskrit: janamejayasya yāṃ rājño vaiśaṃpāyana uktavān yathāvat sa ṛṣis tuṣṭyā satre dvaipāyanājñayā
english: "— which Vaiśaṃpāyana, that ṛṣi, recited duly and with joy to King Janamejaya at the sacrifice, by the command of Dvaipāyana —"

sanskrit: vedaiś caturbhiḥ samitāṃ vyāsasyādbhutakarmaṇaḥ saṃhitāṃ śrotum icchāmo dharmyāṃ pāpabhayāpahām
english: "— we wish to hear that saṃhitā of Vyāsa of wondrous deeds, equal to the four Vedas, righteous and removing the fear of sin."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca ādyaṃ puruṣam īśānaṃ puruhūtaṃ puruṣṭutam ṛtam ekākṣaraṃ brahma vyaktāvyaktaṃ sanātanam
english: The sūta said: "Having made obeisance to the primal Puruṣa, the Lord, invoked by many and praised by many, who is the Truth, the one-syllabled Brahman, both manifest and unmanifest, the eternal —"

sanskrit: asac ca sac caiva ca yad viśvaṃ sadasataḥ param parāvarāṇāṃ sraṣṭāraṃ purāṇaṃ param avyayam
english: "— who is both the unreal and the real, who is this universe, who transcends both being and non-being, the creator of the high and the low, the ancient, the supreme, the imperishable —"

sanskrit: maṅgalyaṃ maṅgalaṃ viṣṇuṃ vareṇyam anaghaṃ śucim namaskṛtya hṛṣīkeśaṃ carācaraguruṃ harim
english: "— having bowed to Viṣṇu, the auspicious source of all auspiciousness, the most excellent, sinless, pure, Hṛṣīkeśa, Hari, the teacher of all that moves and does not move —"

sanskrit: maharṣeḥ pūjitasyeha sarvaloke mahātmanaḥ pravakṣyāmi mataṃ kṛtsnaṃ vyāsasyāmitatejasaḥ
english: "— I shall now fully declare the teaching of Vyāsa of boundless splendour, that great-souled maharṣi honoured throughout all the world."

sanskrit: ācakhyuḥ kavayaḥ ke cit saṃpraty ācakṣate pare ākhyāsyanti tathaivānye itihāsam imaṃ bhuvi
english: "Some poets have told this itihāsa on earth; others are telling it even now; and yet others will tell it likewise in the future."

sanskrit: idaṃ tu triṣu lokeṣu mahaj jñānaṃ pratiṣṭhitam vistaraiś ca samāsaiś ca dhāryate yad dvijātibhiḥ
english: "This great knowledge is established in the three worlds; it is preserved by the twice-born both in its expanded and its condensed forms."

sanskrit: alaṃkṛtaṃ śubhaiḥ śabdaiḥ samayair divyamānuṣaiḥ chandovṛttaiś ca vividhair anvitaṃ viduṣāṃ priyam
english: "Adorned with auspicious words, with divine and human usages, furnished with various metres and verses, it is dear to the learned."

sanskrit: niṣprabhe 'smin nirāloke sarvatas tamasāvṛte bṛhad aṇḍam abhūd ekaṃ prajānāṃ bījam akṣayam
english: "In this state when there was no lustre, no light, when all was enveloped in darkness on every side, there arose the single great Egg, the imperishable seed of all creatures."

sanskrit: yugasyādau nimittaṃ tan mahad divyaṃ pracakṣate yasmiṃs tac chrūyate satyaṃ jyotir brahma sanātanam
english: "At the beginning of the age, that great divine cause is proclaimed; within it is heard the true light, the eternal Brahman."

sanskrit: adbhutaṃ cāpy acintyaṃ ca sarvatra samatāṃ gatam avyaktaṃ kāraṇaṃ sūkṣmaṃ yat tat sadasadātmakam
english: "That which is wondrous and unthinkable, which has attained equality everywhere, unmanifest, subtle, the cause — that is of the nature of both being and non-being."

sanskrit: yasmāt pitāmaho jajñe prabhur ekaḥ prajāpatiḥ brahmā suraguruḥ sthāṇur manuḥ kaḥ parameṣṭhy atha
english: "From that arose the Grandfather, the one Lord, Prajāpati, Brahmā, the teacher of gods, Sthāṇu (Śiva), Manu, Ka, and Parameṣṭhin."

sanskrit: prācetasas tathā dakṣo dakṣaputrāś ca sapta ye tataḥ prajānāṃ patayaḥ prābhavann ekaviṃśatiḥ
english: "Then Dakṣa Prācetasa, and the seven sons of Dakṣa — from these arose the twenty-one lords of creatures."

sanskrit: puruṣaś cāprameyātmā yaṃ sarvam ṛṣayo viduḥ viśvedevās tathādityā vasavo 'thāśvināv api
english: "And the Puruṣa of immeasurable self, whom all the ṛṣis know, the Viśvedevas, the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the two Aśvins as well —"

sanskrit: yakṣāḥ sādhyāḥ piśācāś ca guhyakāḥ pitaras tathā tataḥ prasūtā vidvāṃsaḥ śiṣṭā brahmarṣayo 'malāḥ
english: "— the Yakṣas, Sādhyas, Piśācas, Guhyakas, and the Pitṛs — from these sprang the learned, the well-conducted, the spotless brahmarṣis."

sanskrit: rājarṣayaś ca bahavaḥ sarvaiḥ samuditā guṇaiḥ āpo dyauḥ pṛthivī vāyur antarikṣaṃ diśas tathā
english: "And many royal sages endowed with all virtues; water, sky, earth, wind, the intermediate regions, and the directions —"

sanskrit: saṃvatsarartavo māsāḥ pakṣāhorātrayaḥ kramāt yac cānyad api tat sarvaṃ saṃbhūtaṃ lokasākṣikam
english: "— the year, the seasons, the months, the fortnights, days and nights in succession — and whatever else came into being that is witnessed by the world —"

sanskrit: yad idaṃ dṛśyate kiṃ cid bhūtaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam punaḥ saṃkṣipyate sarvaṃ jagat prāpte yugakṣaye
english: "— whatever is seen here, whether stationary or moving — all this universe is drawn back again at the end of the age."

sanskrit: yathartāv ṛtuliṅgāni nānārūpāṇi paryaye dṛśyante tāni tāny eva tathā bhāvā yugādiṣu
english: "Just as the many and varied marks of the seasons appear again and again in their cycle, so too do conditions recur at the beginnings of each age."

sanskrit: evam etad anādyantaṃ bhūtasaṃhārakārakam anādinidhanaṃ loke cakraṃ saṃparivartate
english: "Thus this wheel, without beginning or end, causing the dissolution of all beings, without beginning or cessation, revolves in the world."

sanskrit: trayastriṃśatsahasrāṇi trayastriṃśacchatāni ca trayastriṃśac ca devānāṃ sṛṣṭiḥ saṃkṣepalakṣaṇā
english: "Thirty-three thousand, thirty-three hundred, and thirty-three — such, in brief, is the count of the creation of the gods."

sanskrit: divasputro bṛhadbhānuś cakṣur ātmā vibhāvasuḥ savitā ca ṛcīko 'rko bhānur āśāvaho raviḥ
english: "Bṛhadbhānu, son of Divas; Cakṣus; Ātmā; Vibhāvasu; Savitā; Ṛcīka; Arka; Bhānu; Āśāvaha; Ravi —"

sanskrit: putrā vivasvataḥ sarve mahyas teṣāṃ tathāvaraḥ devabhrāṭ tanayas tasya tasmāt subhrāḍ iti smṛtaḥ
english: "All these are sons of Vivasvat; among them the youngest was Mahya; Devabhrāṭ was Mahya's son; and from him is born one known as Subhrāṭ."

sanskrit: subhrājas tu trayaḥ putrāḥ prajāvanto bahuśrutāḥ daśajyotiḥ śatajyotiḥ sahasrajyotir ātmavān
english: "Subhrāṭ had three sons, bearers of offspring and greatly learned: Daśajyoti, Śatajyoti, and the self-possessed Sahasrajyoti."

sanskrit: daśa putrasahasrāṇi daśajyoter mahātmanaḥ tato daśaguṇāś cānye śatajyoter ihātmajāḥ
english: "The great-souled Daśajyoti had ten thousand sons; the sons of Śatajyoti here numbered ten times that many."

sanskrit: bhūyas tato daśaguṇāḥ sahasrajyotiṣaḥ sutāḥ tebhyo 'yaṃ kuruvaṃśaś ca yadūnāṃ bharatasya ca
english: "And the sons of Sahasrajyoti were ten times greater still; from them arose this lineage of the Kurus, of the Yadus, and of Bharata."

sanskrit: yayātīkṣvākuvaṃśaś ca rājarṣīṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ saṃbhūtā bahavo vaṃśā bhūtasargāḥ savistarāḥ
english: "And the lineages of Yayāti and Ikṣvāku, and of royal sages in every direction — many dynasties and the detailed creation of beings arose from them."

sanskrit: bhūtasthānāni sarvāṇi rahasyaṃ trividhaṃ ca yat vedayogaṃ savijñānaṃ dharmo 'rthaḥ kāma eva ca
english: "All the abodes of beings, the threefold secret, the application of the Vedas together with its knowledge, dharma, artha, and kāma as well —"

sanskrit: dharmakāmārthaśāstrāṇi śāstrāṇi vividhāni ca lokayātrāvidhānaṃ ca saṃbhūtaṃ dṛṣṭavān ṛṣiḥ
english: "— the śāstras of dharma, kāma, and artha, the various other śāstras, and the ordinances for the conduct of worldly life — all this the ṛṣi saw and set down."

sanskrit: itihāsāḥ savaiyākhyā vividhāḥ śrutayo 'pi ca iha sarvam anukrāntam uktaṃ granthasya lakṣaṇam
english: "Itihāsas with commentaries, and the various śrutis as well — all of this is traversed here; such is declared to be the scope of this text."

sanskrit: vistīryaitan mahaj jñānam ṛṣiḥ saṃkṣepam abravīt iṣṭaṃ hi viduṣāṃ loke samāsavyāsadhāraṇam
english: "Having expanded this great knowledge, the ṛṣi also stated it in condensed form; for in the world, both the expanded and the condensed forms are cherished by the learned."

sanskrit: manvādi bhārataṃ ke cid āstīkādi tathāpare tathoparicarādy anye viprāḥ samyag adhīyate
english: "Some brāhmaṇas study the Bhārata beginning from the Manu episode, others from the Āstīka episode, and still others from the Uparicara episode — each according to his tradition."

sanskrit: vividhaṃ saṃhitājñānaṃ dīpayanti manīṣiṇaḥ vyākhyātuṃ kuśalāḥ ke cid granthaṃ dhārayituṃ pare
english: "The wise illuminate the various knowledge of the saṃhitā; some are skilled in expounding the text, others in preserving it."

sanskrit: tapasā brahmacaryeṇa vyasya vedaṃ sanātanam itihāsam imaṃ cakre puṇyaṃ satyavatīsutaḥ
english: "By austerity and celibate study, having arranged the eternal Veda, the son of Satyavatī composed this holy itihāsa."

sanskrit: parāśarātmajo vidvān brahmarṣiḥ saṃśitavrataḥ mātur niyogād dharmātmā gāṅgeyasya ca dhīmataḥ
english: "The learned son of Parāśara, the brahmarṣi of sharpened vow, righteous of soul, at the bidding of his mother and of the wise Gāṅgeya —"

sanskrit: kṣetre vicitravīryasya kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaḥ purā trīn agnīn iva kauravyāñ janayām āsa vīryavān
english: "— the mighty Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana formerly fathered, in the field of Vicitravīrya, three offspring of the Kuru line, like three sacred fires."

sanskrit: utpādya dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ ca pāṇḍuṃ viduram eva ca jagāma tapase dhīmān punar evāśramaṃ prati
english: "Having begotten Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu, and Vidura, the wise one returned once more to his hermitage for austerities."

sanskrit: teṣu jāteṣu vṛddheṣu gateṣu paramāṃ gatim abravīd bhārataṃ loke mānuṣe 'smin mahān ṛṣiḥ
english: "When those three were born, had grown up, and had gone to the highest state, that great ṛṣi proclaimed the Bhārata in this human world."

sanskrit: janamejayena pṛṣṭaḥ san brāhmaṇaiś ca sahasraśaḥ śaśāsa śiṣyam āsīnaṃ vaiśaṃpāyanam antike
english: "Being asked by Janamejaya and by thousands of brāhmaṇas, he instructed his disciple Vaiśaṃpāyana, who was seated nearby."

sanskrit: sa sadasyaiḥ sahāsīnaḥ śrāvayām āsa bhāratam karmāntareṣu yajñasya codyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: "Seated together with the officiants, Vaiśaṃpāyana caused the Bhārata to be heard, being urged again and again during the intervals of the sacrifice."

sanskrit: vistaraṃ kuruvaṃśasya gāndhāryā dharmaśīlatām kṣattuḥ prajñāṃ dhṛtiṃ kuntyāḥ samyag dvaipāyano 'bravīt
english: "Dvaipāyana properly told of the full extent of the Kuru lineage, the righteousness of Gāndhārī, the wisdom of Kṣattṛ (Vidura), and the fortitude of Kuntī."

sanskrit: vāsudevasya māhātmyaṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca satyatām durvṛttaṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇām uktavān bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
english: "The blessed ṛṣi told of the greatness of Vāsudeva, the truthfulness of the Pāṇḍavas, and the evil conduct of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra."

sanskrit: caturviṃśatisāhasrīṃ cakre bhāratasaṃhitām upākhyānair vinā tāvad bhārataṃ procyate budhaiḥ
english: "He composed the Bhārata saṃhitā of twenty-four thousand verses; without the subsidiary tales, that much is called the Bhārata by the learned."

sanskrit: tato 'dhyardhaśataṃ bhūyaḥ saṃkṣepaṃ kṛtavān ṛṣiḥ anukramaṇim adhyāyaṃ vṛttāntānāṃ saparvaṇām
english: "After that, the ṛṣi further made a condensed version of one hundred and fifty verses, the index chapter that summarises the contents along with the parvans."

sanskrit: idaṃ dvaipāyanaḥ pūrvaṃ putram adhyāpayac chukam tato 'nyebhyo 'nurūpebhyaḥ śiṣyebhyaḥ pradadau prabhuḥ
english: "Dvaipāyana first taught this to his son Śuka; thereafter the lord gave it to other fitting disciples as well."

sanskrit: nārado 'śrāvayad devān asito devalaḥ pitṝn gandharvayakṣarakṣāṃsi śrāvayām āsa vai śukaḥ
english: "Nārada caused the gods to hear it; Asita Devala caused the Pitṛs to hear it; and Śuka caused the Gandharvas, Yakṣas, and Rākṣasas to hear it."

sanskrit: duryodhano manyumayo mahādrumaḥ; skandhaḥ karṇaḥ śakunis tasya śākhāḥ duḥśāsanaḥ puṣpaphale samṛddhe; mūlaṃ rājā dhṛtarāṣṭro 'manīṣī
english: "Duryodhana is a great tree made of wrath; Karṇa is its trunk; Śakuni its branches; Duḥśāsana its abundant flowers and fruit; and the unwise King Dhṛtarāṣṭra is its root."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiro dharmamayo mahādrumaḥ; skandho 'rjuno bhīmaseno 'sya śākhāḥ mādrīsutau puṣpaphale samṛddhe; mūlaṃ kṛṣṇo brahma ca brāhmaṇāś ca
english: "Yudhiṣṭhira is a great tree made of dharma; Arjuna is its trunk; Bhīmasena its branches; the twin sons of Mādrī its abundant flowers and fruit; and Kṛṣṇa, Brahman, and the brāhmaṇas are its root."

sanskrit: pāṇḍur jitvā bahūn deśān yudhā vikramaṇena ca araṇye mṛgayāśīlo nyavasat sajanas tadā
english: "Pāṇḍu, having conquered many lands by warfare and valour, lived in the forest devoted to hunting, along with his people."

sanskrit: mṛgavyavāyanidhane kṛcchrāṃ prāpa sa āpadam janmaprabhṛti pārthānāṃ tatrācāravidhikramaḥ
english: "By killing a deer in the act of mating, he incurred a terrible calamity; and it was there that the Pārthas were born and the sequence of their customs and conduct began."

sanskrit: mātror abhyupapattiś ca dharmopaniṣadaṃ prati dharmasya vāyoḥ śakrasya devayoś ca tathāśvinoḥ
english: "And the assistance of the two mothers with regard to the mystery of dharma — the approach of Dharma, Vāyu, Śakra, and likewise of the two divine Aśvins —"

sanskrit: tāpasaiḥ saha saṃvṛddhā mātṛbhyāṃ parirakṣitāḥ medhyāraṇyeṣu puṇyeṣu mahatām āśrameṣu ca
english: "— growing up together with ascetics, protected by their mothers, in sacred pure forests and in the hermitages of the great ones —"

sanskrit: ṛṣibhiś ca tadānītā dhārtarāṣṭrān prati svayam śiśavaś cābhirūpāś ca jaṭilā brahmacāriṇaḥ
english: "— and the children, handsome, with matted hair, living as celibate students, were then personally brought by the ṛṣis to the Dhārtarāṣṭras —"

sanskrit: putrāś ca bhrātaraś ceme śiṣyāś ca suhṛdaś ca vaḥ pāṇḍavā eta ity uktvā munayo 'ntarhitās tataḥ
english: "— and saying 'These are your sons, brothers, disciples, and friends — these are the Pāṇḍavas,' the sages then vanished."

sanskrit: tāṃs tair niveditān dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍavān kauravās tadā śiṣṭāś ca varṇāḥ paurā ye te harṣāc cukruśur bhṛśam
english: "Seeing the Pāṇḍavas presented by them, the Kauravas at that time, and the well-born citizens of all the classes, cried out repeatedly in great joy."

sanskrit: āhuḥ ke cin na tasyaite tasyaita iti cāpare yadā ciramṛtaḥ pāṇḍuḥ kathaṃ tasyeti cāpare
english: "Some said, 'These are not his sons'; others said, 'They are indeed his.' Still others said, 'Since Pāṇḍu died long ago, how can they be his?'"

sanskrit: svāgataṃ sarvathā diṣṭyā pāṇḍoḥ paśyāma saṃtatim ucyatāṃ svāgatam iti vāco 'śrūyanta sarvaśaḥ
english: "Voices were heard everywhere saying: 'Welcome — by good fortune we behold the offspring of Pāṇḍu! Let welcome be declared!'"

sanskrit: tasminn uparate śabde diśaḥ sarvā vinādayan antarhitānāṃ bhūtānāṃ nisvanas tumulo 'bhavat
english: "When that noise died down, a tumultuous sound arose from unseen beings, filling all the directions."

sanskrit: puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ śubhā gandhāḥ śaṅkhadundubhinisvanāḥ āsan praveśe pārthānāṃ tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: "At the entry of the Pārthas there was a rain of flowers, auspicious fragrances, and the sound of conches and drums — it seemed wondrous."

sanskrit: tatprītyā caiva sarveṣāṃ paurāṇāṃ harṣasaṃbhavaḥ śabda āsīn mahāṃs tatra divaspṛk kīrtivardhanaḥ
english: "And out of the joy of all the citizens, a great joyous sound arose there that touched the sky and magnified their glory."

sanskrit: te 'py adhītyākhilān vedāñ śāstrāṇi vividhāni ca nyavasan pāṇḍavās tatra pūjitā akutobhayāḥ
english: "And those Pāṇḍavas, having studied all the Vedas and the various śāstras, dwelt there honoured and without fear from any quarter."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhirasya śaucena prītāḥ prakṛtayo 'bhavan dhṛtyā ca bhīmasenasya vikrameṇārjunasya ca
english: "The subjects were gladdened by the purity of Yudhiṣṭhira, by the steadfastness of Bhīmasena, and by the valour of Arjuna —"
